definitions.explanation: The state or moment of having just woken up. Describes the groggy period immediately after waking from sleep.

definitions.gloss: sleeping and waking, daily life in a place
definitions.explanation: The routine of sleeping and getting up, often used to describe where one lives or stays.

examples.japanese: {寝起|ねお}きの{顔|かお}を{見|み}られたくない。
examples.english: I don't want people to see my face right after waking up.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{寝起|ねお}きがいいので、{目覚|めざ}ましなしで{起|お}きられる。
examples.english: He wakes up easily, so he can get up without an alarm.

examples.japanese: ここで{寝起|ねお}きしている。
examples.english: I live here (sleep and wake here).

examples.japanese: {学生|がくせい}{時代|じだい}は{友人|ゆうじん}のアパートで{寝起|ねお}きしていた。
examples.english: During my student days, I was living at a friend's apartment.

examples.japanese: {狭|せま}い{部屋|へや}で{三人|さんにん}が{寝起|ねお}きしていた。
examples.english: Three people were living in a small room.

notes:
USAGE:
The most common usage is in the phrase {寝起|ねお}きがいい／{悪|わる}い, describing whether someone wakes up easily or with difficulty.
In sense 2, {寝起|ねお}き takes する to form a verb meaning to sleep and get up (i.e., to live or stay somewhere).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {寝起|ねお}きがいい — to be a good waker, to wake up easily
- {寝起|ねお}きが{悪|わる}い — to be a bad waker, to have trouble waking up
- {寝起|ねお}きの{顔|かお} — face just after waking
- {寝起|ねお}きする — to sleep and wake (live somewhere)
